Syllabary 1: one sign per syllable; the vowels Ꭰ Ꭱ Ꭲ Ꭳ Ꭴ Ꭵ and the g / k and h rows
Syllabary 2: the l, m, n and gw rows, with Ꮏ hna and Ꮐ nah
lessons.deck: Syllabary: l, m, n and gw

lessons.title: Syllabary 3: the s row with lone Ꮝ s, and the d / t and dl / tl rows
Syllabary 4: the ts, w and y rows; reading whole words and what the syllabary leaves unwritten
Greetings: ᎣᏏᏲ, ᏙᎯᏧ?, ᏙᎯᏊ, ᏩᏙ, ᏛᎬᎪᎯ
First words: ᎥᎥ (yes), ᎥᏝ / Ꮭ (no), ᎰᏩ (okay), ᎣᏍᏓ (good), ᏣᎳᎩ
Numbers 1-10: ᏌᏊ, ᏔᎵ, ᏦᎢ, ᏅᎩ, ᎯᏍᎩ … ᏍᎪᎯ
Names: ᏓᏆᏙᎠ (… is what I am called), ᎦᏙ ᏕᏣᏙᎠ? (what are you called?)
ᎠᏴ (I, we), ᏂᎯ (you), ᎯᎠ (this one here), ᎥᏍᎩᎾ (that one there), Ꮎ; and ᎠᏂ (here), ᎤᎿ (there)
Question words ᎦᏙ (what), ᎦᎪ (who), ᎯᎳ ᎢᎦ? (how many) and the question endings -Ꮝ / -ᏍᎪ
Numbers to 100: ᏌᏚ (11), ᏔᎵᏍᎪᎯ (20), ᏍᎪᎯᏥᏆ (100)
Verbs are sentences: ᎠᎪᏩᏘᎭ (he sees him / it), ᎠᏂᎪᏩᏘᎭ (they see him / it)
Set A prefixes: ᏥᎪᏩᏘᎭ (I see him / it), ᎯᎪᏩᏘᎭ (you see him / it)
Colours: ᎤᏁᎦ (white), ᎩᎦᎨᎢ (red), ᎬᎿᎨᎢ (black), ᏌᎪᏂᎨᎢ (blue), ᏓᎶᏂᎨᎢ (yellow)
Plurals by prefix: ᎠᏍᎦᏯ / ᎠᏂᏍᎦᏯ (man / men), ᎦᏍᎩᎶ / ᏗᎦᏍᎩᎶ (table or chair / tables or chairs)
Set B prefixes: ᎠᏆᏚᎵᎭ (I want it), ᏣᏚᎵᎭ (you want it), ᎤᏚᎵᎭ (he wants it), ᎤᎾᏚᎵᎭ (they want it)
Saying "not": Ꮭ with the Ᏹ- prefix (Ꮭ ᏱᎩ, Ꮭ ᏯᎩᎭ, Ꮭ ᏳᎭ)
"Have" depends on the thing: ᎠᎩᎭ (I have it, solid), ᎠᎩᎧᎭ (I have it, alive)
Animals and counting living things: ᎩᏟ, ᏪᏌ, ᎠᎭᏫ, ᏩᎭᏯ, ᏲᎾ; ᎢᏯᏂ
Is and was: ᎢᎩ, ᎢᎦ, ᎨᏒᎩ (I saw it), ᎨᏎᎢ (I was told)

decks.name: Syllabary: vowels, g/k and h
decks.desc: The six vowel signs and the g / k and h rows, one card per sign (19 cards).

decks.name: Syllabary: l, m, n and gw
decks.desc: The l, m, n (with Ꮏ hna, Ꮐ nah) and gw rows, one card per sign (25 cards).

decks.name: Syllabary: s, d/t and dl/tl
decks.desc: The s row with lone Ꮝ, the d / t row and the dl / tl row, one card per sign (23 cards).

decks.name: Syllabary: ts, w and y
decks.desc: The ts, w and y rows, one card per sign (18 cards); Ᏽ mv is archaic and left out.

decks.name: Greetings
decks.desc: Hello, how are you, I'm fine, thanks, and "I will see you again".

decks.name: First words
decks.desc: Yes, no, okay, good and bad, and, but, Cherokee and English.

decks.name: Names and introductions
decks.desc: "… is what I am called", "what are you called?", and Cherokee forms of English names.

decks.name: Pronouns, questions and places
decks.desc: I, you, this one, that one; what, who, which, how many; here, there, near, far.

decks.name: Numbers 1 to 10
decks.desc: Zero to ten, "how many?" for things and for living beings, two and three for people.

decks.name: Numbers to 100
decks.desc: Eleven to nineteen, the tens and a hundred.

decks.name: People
decks.desc: Woman, man, girl, boy, person, Cherokee and English people: one and many.

decks.name: Animals and things
decks.desc: Dog, cat, deer, wolf, bear, horse, rabbit; rock, tree, potato, beans, paper, table.

decks.name: Colours
decks.desc: White, red, black, blue, yellow, purple, brown, green, and the faded mixes.

decks.name: Seeing (Set A)
decks.desc: One word for "he sees it", "I see him", "you see them": the Set A forms of the verb "see".

decks.name: Wanting (Set B)
decks.desc: I want it, you want it, he wants it, they want it: the Set B forms of the verb "want".

decks.name: Having: solid and alive
decks.desc: "Have" for a solid thing (ᎠᎩᎭ) and for a living one (ᎠᎩᎧᎭ), with "have them".

decks.name: Not, is and was
decks.desc: Is now, is usually, was (seen or told), will be, and isn't.

decks.name: Traps for English speakers
decks.desc: The prefix that shows how many and what kind, solid against alive, Ꮭ with Ᏹ-, and the question endings.
